regime.summary: The SBP hiked 100bp on 2026-04-27 to 11.5% while CPI roughly doubled in three months to 10.91% and Brent is up 46.9%. The index is -8.9% over 3m but +65.3% over 12m. Real policy rate is only about 0.6pp. Closest analogues are tightening-plus-external-stress episodes, which fell hard, but a first hike has only n=2 and no timing edge, so I trim rather than exit.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 11.5%; last MPC decision 2026-04-27: hike (+100bp)
CPI YoY 10.91% for 2026-04 (published by 2026-05-03); three months earlier (2026-01) 5.79%
Tightening plus external stress: rate up 800bp in ten months with CPI above it.

core.thesis: Holding company priced at 5.1x earnings with quarterly EPS up 4.27x year on year, close to its 252-day high while the index fell over 3m. Relative strength in a falling market. Business questions B1, B3 and B13 (growth, not mere stability) are the test; the EPS jump may include one-offs, so I size at 20 not more.

evidence.quote: B13. Is it growing, not merely stable?

core.thesis: The oil link I actually hold, with Brent up 46.9% in 3m while the E&P sector's 3m return is still negative. Quarterly EPS up 31.1% year on year at 11.5x. Hedges the oil and inflation leg of the regime risk inside the core. Dividend yield is low priority; case is earnings growth.

evidence.quote: A8. Oil: where is Brent, and which link do I actually hold?

core.thesis: Quarterly EPS up 54.1% year on year at 6.0x earnings with a 1.5% yield, so profits are retained to compound. Price is 15% below its 252-day high after a 25.8% one-month jump, so it is extended short term; I accept that and size below the other two. Sponsor quality is not in the bundle (B5, B6 unanswered).

evidence.quote: B6. How does the sponsor treat minorities?

watch.subject: Next MPC decision and monthly CPI
watch.trigger: Add toward the 75% core default when CPI stops rising and the SBP holds; cut further if another hike lands with CPI still accelerating.

evidence.quote: Regime: 6M T-bill minus policy rate +0.48pp (market near policy rate); CPI rising over 3 months (+5.1pp)
Lesson: hold bills, and set a trigger to return.

watch.subject: PSO
watch.trigger: Quarterly EPS up 6.8x yet price is -24.6% over 3m; enter only if price confirms and P/E case holds, since muted reaction above 6x P/E has a poor measured record.

watch.subject: SGPL
watch.trigger: Seven upper locks in 10 days and +193% in 1m. Measured record for this type is nothing; do not chase, revisit only if the filings explain the move.

watch.subject: NETSOL
watch.trigger: Quarterly EPS up 3.39x with a revoked then revised material-information notice on 2026-05-04; wait for the revised disclosure to be understood before sizing.

exposure_reason: Below the 75% default because a 100bp hike, CPI doubling in 3m and Brent up 47% match the tightening-plus-stress analogues, where the median stock fell hard; the 20 points held back is dry powder for the MPC/CPI trigger. Not lower because no timing edge exists for a first hike (n=2), real rates are only about 0.6pp, and the core rests on business questions.
not_known: FX reserves and current account, IMF status, political risk, sponsor and balance-sheet quality of the core names, and the next MPC date are not in the bundle. EPS growth may contain one-offs.
contamination_note: I have a training cutoff after this date; I noticed no recalled post-2026-05-08 facts and used only the bundle. The base_rates.csv warning says it is measured partly after this date, so I used it only as rough type-level odds.
